messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: p99 latency breach detected for customer SiloApps (single-tenant) in us-east-1. Current p99 = 6.2s, p95 = 1.8s. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming). Pager: @Maya (oncall).
Maya (oncall): acked. I'm looking. Do we have any alerts showing concurrent sessions or recent deploys?
PagerDuty Bot: Alert details: metric=tail_latency.p99, threshold=5s, window=5m, max_concurrency=780. No deploys in last 30m.
Michelle (cs): Customer on-call says they started a batch of UI tests ~2m before alert, simulating lots of long context prompts. They're seeing stalls in streaming frames.
Leo (sre): grabbing traces. Initial look: spikes correlate with a small subset of requests with very long prefixes (5k+ tokens) + repeated identical warmup prompt. Could be hotprefix thrash.
Ricardo (infra): The dedicated pool for SiloApps is at 92% utilization. Autoscaler didn't trigger due to short spike patterns; instance spinup latency ~45s.
Ash (eng-runtime): Noted. Runtime logs show a sharp rise in KV cache evictions for that tenant around 4300012300. Eviction rate x10 baseline -> leads to repeated recompute of KV segments and stall on first streaming frames.
Maya (oncall): mitigation options: (1) immediately throttle concurrent sessions for SiloApps, (2) route a portion of traffic to their fallback model (smaller/quant), (3) scale pool manually. Which is fastest?
Leo (sre): Manual scale is fastest if we can hot-add GPUs from spare capacity — Ricardo can we do that now?
Ricardo (infra): We have 2 spare machines in us-east-1 but they need driver sync. I can allocate and force-add to the pool; ETA 90s to attach + 30s to warm.
Ash (eng-runtime): Fallback to quantized model is instant from routing config (policy-based). Quality will degrade but streaming latency should drop. Also we can enable prefix-KV sticky caching for this tenant to reduce churn (requires a config flip, instant but may increase memory).
Maya (oncall): Action plan: 1) Michelle please ask customer to pause synthetic UI tests for 10m (mitigate storm). 2) Ricardo, add 1 spare GPU to dedicated pool now. 3) Ash, flip routing to fallback quant model for 20% of requests and enable prefix sticky cache for SiloApps. 4) Leo continue tracing root cause.
Michelle (cs): Messaged SiloApps. They paused tests and confirmed.
Ricardo (infra): attaching GPU now. Command run: ```infractl pool attach --pool silo-dedicated --instance i-0a12bbcc --fast-attach```
Ricardo (infra): GPU attached. Pool capacity +1. Adding to autoscale group, nodes show joining.
Ash (eng-runtime): Flipped routing: 20% -> model-s6-quant; enabled prefixStickyCache=true for tenant=siloapps. Watch logs for failures.
Leo (sre): traces after mitigations: p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 2.4s within 40s. p95 down to 1.1s. Streaming frame stall counts decreased significantly.
Maya (oncall): Good. Still seeing some sustained p99 ~2.4s. Is that acceptable to declare in-progress mitigation? We should keep paging until p99 < 1.5s for 10m.
Ash (eng-runtime): We see some residual stalls from requests that had already lost KV cache and are replaying long prefixes; those sessions will finish out. Future requests are improved.
Ricardo (infra): Autoscaler review: current policy uses 1m window; we should consider lowering to 30s for single-tenant high-fanout customers. Filed infra ticket: INFRA-1129.
Leo (sre): Root cause hypothesis: customer-generated hotprompt patterns create cache churn (many unique long prefixes) combined with high concurrency -> KV cache thrash -> sequential recomputation blocking streaming generator on first frames leading to p99 spikes.
Maya (oncall): Risks/next steps: - Keep 20% fallback for 10m. - Leave prefixStickyCache for 1h while we monitor memory. - If p99 doesn't stabilize <1.5s, scale pool +1 more. - Assign investigation to Leo + Ash for follow-up.
Michelle (cs): Customer confirmed they will throttle their UI tests and will report back in 15m. They appreciated the fallback approach.
Leo (sre): creating ticket SRE-8904: "SiloApps tail latency - hotprefix KV thrash analysis". Adding traces, flamegraphs, and sample prompt payloads.
Ash (eng-runtime): quick log excerpt: ```[4300012298] tenant=siloapps kvcache:evict=1234 miss=950 hit=12 regen=0 blocking_ms=3500``` 
Maya (oncall): handoff: I'm handing off to Leo (sre) for deep-dive post-mitigation. I'll stay available for escalation. Marking this thread in #oncall-handoff.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident status changed: acknowledged -> mitigated (partial).
Ricardo (infra): note: adjusted autoscaler vars in staging to test 30s sensitivity. If validated, we can push to prod.
Leo (sre): will run replay tests with copied payloads in staging to reproduce cache thrash. Also will run KV cache warm strategy and measure improvement.
Maya (oncall): update in 10m. If p99 holds <1.5s for next 10m, we'll resolve page and start postmortem. :white_check_mark:
Michelle (cs): customer reports UI flowing again. Thanks all.
Leo (sre): 10m check: p99 = 1.3s, p95 = 0.9s, error rate normal. Closing page in 5m unless regression.
Maya (oncall): closing page in 5. Follow-ups: SRE-8904 (investigate kv eviction policy), ENG-PRIORITY: runtime sticky-cache TTL option, INFRA-1129 (autoscale window). Assign owners: Leo, Ash, Ricardo.
Maya (oncall): final: incident classified as "SLO breach (p99) due to tenant-induced KV cache thrash; mitigated via capacity and routing fallback". Postmortem assigned to Leo.
incident-bot: Incident closed by Maya (oncall) at 4300012578."
